Above, below, and all around, it is transparently free of boundaries or peripheries. Draw near to it and it becomes ever more distant; distance yourself from it and it becomes ever more near.
Seeking the center within that [center], it lies a thousand li away before one's very face. Strive on, O Yuanzhong! Please take these words to heart.
Regarding the Head Seat Jian Jingyuan (whose style name is Ming):
stillness is the substance of movement, and movement is the function of stillness. When both movement and stillness are embraced together, every action is centered. If you wish to know its stillness:

If you wish to investigate its movement, you must examine its source; if you wish to know its activity, you must examine its root. When examined to the point where there is nothing further to examine, it stands alone, transcendent and solitary.
Like clouds drifting through the sky or water rushing into a ravine—what intention do they have to become rapids or cranes? It is the single, true Dharma-realm.
Nothing is not harmoniously integrated within it. In motion and in stillness, the tigers of the Teachings and the dragons of Chan laugh together at the inscription on the screen.
How great is this screen! Vast, transparent, and unobstructed—sitting in meditation within it, one attains great sovereignty. Green mountains rest upon the desk before one.
Green waters face the gate; together we laugh and converse, without ceasing from dawn to dusk. The ten thousand phenomena nod their heads; the thousand sages lean in to listen.
If you ask who it is that laughs, the sword has long since departed. Yangqi opens his mouth; Kāśyapa breaks into a smile. He falls by himself and rises by himself.
Striving to penetrate the heavy barrier, tearing asunder the single transmission, overturning the direct pointing—this is the inexhaustible Dharma-treasury. This very carriage is it:
using the constant to inscribe the constant, and using while remaining constantly constant. Without interior or exterior, there is a standard and a measure. What is meant by "constant"?
Tranquil and great samādhi—what is meant by its "functioning"? It is the single essence manifesting in myriad responses; it functions yet is not functioning, it is constant yet is not constant.
It is profoundly still and silent, yet luminously intelligent. I address you, O Great Man: clear away all delusions and falsehoods. Even a cowpen or a stable [is but a manifestation of this].
The Great Treasury of Radiance:

Chief Seat Qi’s "Inscription on the Name 'Wuzhi' (No Dependence)" states that True Illumination is wondrously perfect; it neither turns its back nor faces forward, standing solitary and detached. How could it rely upon external support? It is like clouds emerging from mountain peaks.
Like a bird soaring through the sky, carefree and sovereign—how could one seek its tracks? How could a person of wisdom rely on this single point?
The great earth sinks flat, and Mount Sumeru stands overturned.
The Inscription for the West Hall’s “Hidden in the West” (Xīyǐn):
The Dharma of the Mind is formless, encompassing all things. Hidden yet not manifest, it is revealed in its stark clarity, extending throughout the four quarters, above, and below.
Impartiality knows no deficiency; the mind pervades all within it—how could it be confined to a single direction or corner? In the past, there was Master Liang, who attained the subtlety of the Way.
He concealed his traces on the Western Mountains, and thus his name was summoned by all. To say he was in concealment is not so, for his fame has never decayed;
yet to say he was not in concealment is also not so, for his physical presence vanished without a trace. Who among these bodhisattvas is this? His name is Liang, yet he is hidden in the West.
As for those who use written characters, they truly wish to race alongside [the truth], yet how could they do more than merely follow in its wake? How earnest, how earnest!
It cannot be transmitted or received; to explain it with clarity only serves to add further conceptual traps.
Two *Yújiā'áo* (Fisherman’s Haughton) Poems:
Having read the *Yújiā'áo* presented by Chan Master Kōng of Dōngshān to Mèngshí, I have composed these following its rhyme to mourn Master Miàomíng of Jìngshān.
Although the diction and meaning do not match, the warbling of spring birds and the chirping of autumn insects each find their own expression.
It cries forth at that very moment.

The lineage transmitted through the generations is truly vast and boundless; the Dragon Abyss increases its clarity and stillness for ten thousand ages. The ancient mirror is traceless and brilliantly lucid—deep and profound.
Its light swallows the myriad phenomena, making heaven and earth seem small. The phoenix has departed, leaving only the chirping of common birds in the empty courtyard.
The dew is cold upon the wutong trees at dawn. Those who guide others along the Great Way are now few. Who shall serve as a model? Seeking the path by groping in the dark—when will this ever end?
The fourfold eloquence flows on vast and boundless; failing to exhaust its source and course, my anxious heart is silent. What is this delusive cloud that deceives the sun?
Brilliant! Though it may seem distant and obscure, the lofty clarity is not obscured by minor mists. He dwells alone by the empty pond, taking pity on the birds;

he does not realize that fish are swimming beneath his feet. Life and death are pure and true, lacking nothing. Transcending the mundane world, the transmission of the robe and bowl relies upon those who carry it forward.
Verses compiled for the study of the Dharma by the bhikṣus Qing Sui and others,
presented to the Zen practitioner Xiu.

Nan and Neng were disciples of the same master; morning attendance and evening inquiry occurred at the same time. Why then did you divide the school into North and South, like siblings turning against one another?
It was merely because of differences in their realization of nature; yet in the end, it is known there is but one teaching.
The bright mirror is not a stand, and bubbles arise within fire; the Bodhi tree is but a stake in empty space. How could a man of true character ever consent to this?
The Master [placed it] in his heart; he then descended from the land into the sweet, level depths. Truly, he followed the current to understand the source and its tributaries.
Seeking a sympathetic soul beyond the teachings of the Three Vehicles, the old man in the empty room has no clever wits left. Sometimes while eating, he forgets his chopsticks.
Because you sought words of praise at dawn, I took up my brush and unconsciously wrote this long verse.
A Gift to Master Gao, following the rhyme of Master Nantang:
Zen is not Zen, the Way is not the Way; At midnight, the sun rises in the west at the hour of Mao. Lifting up empty space, one looks at its back.

Four times seven, twenty-three; they are all but a confused and bustling crowd. Selling hats and judging heads, selling flour mixed with bran—those with sweet lips and eloquent tongues are found everywhere.
To stir up the Great Matter and proclaim the School of the Patriarchs is not to say it does not exist at all, yet alas, such people are still few.
Do you not see? Dongshan, in his dealings with others, once descended into the weeds; sea-moon and mountain-clouds both laughed themselves silly. A single song, sung aloud.
A boat descending the river; whose ears can endure its rare and piercing resonance? I inform you: cease your further seeking! The Patriarch’s profound intent shatters the straw sandals;
it is better to go barefoot than to wear fine ones.
I present this "Account of the Nature" for the attendant Xing.

Nature is fundamentally without nature; transmission is fundamentally without transmission. As soon as one engages in conceptual deliberation, one is already a hundred thousand eight thousand leagues away.

It is like water flowing through the earth or fire passing from one piece of wood to another: though the wood may be exhausted, the fire ever blazes on; though the earth may reach its limit, the water returns.

Ting-ting! A father cannot give it to his son; a ruler cannot give it to his minister. Encompassing all existence throughout past and present, one must be a person capable of bearing this burden upon their own shoulders.
Do you not see? When the Vulture Peak faced the assembly and held up a flower, the clouds across the eight directions cleared and the morning sun hung suspended.
And do you not see? At the end of the Shao-lin period, the skin and marrow were divided; at the Dragon Gate, the dragon transforms as the thunder burns its tail.

To say that one's nature can be transmitted is like a silkworm making a cocoon, only to entangle itself in vain. To say that one's nature cannot be transmitted is exactly like digging through the earth in search of the blue sky.
When the mind of a practitioner of the Way is fierce and sharp, once the point is attained, both correctness and partiality vanish.

Whether moving forward or backward, whether with or against the current—what need is there to apply the whip again? With paper robes torn away to reveal bare bones, one stands solitary and vast, far surpassing the time before the Awakened Sound (Vibhāṣā).
Presented to the Physician-Monk Yueke during Illness I harbor the illness of the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
it is not merely my own person that is ill. While the illnesses of the three realms may come to an end, my illness has no final limit.
Ke-t'ing understands the treatment of illness; let me briefly discuss the efficacy of treating disease. The body of illness is empty space, yet the body of illness is separate from empty space.
The moaning laughs at the illness, and the joyous illness laughs at the "I. One pushes away the illness but the illness does not depart; one seeks the illness but the illness leaves no trace.

In recent years, I have recognized the source of illness; I no longer hang this sickness upon my breast. A thousand illnesses and ten thousand ailments are all one and the same as that single illness.
Where there is a body, there is illness; without a body, from where could illness arise?

I present to Master Xiang the Unsurpassed Great Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. This is not something that can be known through mere clever intelligence; it requires a thorough clearing away from the very beginning, until there is absolutely nothing left—not even a hair’s breadth or a speck of dust.
Have you not seen how the Duke of Changli was once tested in the inner quarters by Master Dadian? Only after he had entered [the state of realization]...
From the side of the attendant, first move with meditative concentration and subsequently extract with wisdom. Furthermore, Huang Taishi was never seen;

once he drew near to Heitang to exhaustively investigate his own self, and a gust of western wind brought forth the fragrance of the osmanthus blossoms, only then did he believe that "I have nothing hidden from you.

These two venerable patriarchs were masters for a hundred generations; they fathomed the very marrow within the bones of Shaolin. Those who attain realization follow divergent paths yet belong to one family. Not...

One who has attained stability must surely distinguish between self and other. Master Xiang, Master Xiang, you are well-versed in doing good. Within the gate of the patch-robed monks, there is no mystery or subtlety.
Suddenly grasping one’s own nostrils as they were born from one’s mother, Mount Sumeru is hidden within the hollow of a lotus fiber.
I see Attendant Xi off on a journey to Mount Tiantai and Mount Yan.
The heights of Mount Tiantai are loftily high; the depths of the Dragon Pool are profoundly deep. So deep that they cannot be fathomed by the intellect;
so high that they cannot be measured by the cubit. With dragon bowls and tiger staffs, they explore the wonders and admire the excellence, coming and going in ceaseless succession.

Among those who dwell therein, they cannot be counted by the hundreds. Having harbored a chronic ailment for the misty clouds and mists, and maintaining a life of empty stillness, there have been those from ancient times until now who could not be cured by the medicine of the bodhicitta; such is the tradition of the Way that has passed away.
The profound depths of his breast are cleared; the numinous birds speak by day, singing the wondrous melody of non-arising. The pine wind resounds at night, playing the lute of primordial antiquity.
One by one, let these pass before you; be careful not to discard gold while picking up weeds. Tread through your straw sandals until your feet are bare;
wherever you meet, who would not be a connoisseur?
Sending off my Dharma-nephew Wei as he begins his travels through the Tai and Yan Mountains:
The heights of Tai and the heights of Yan—Heaven’s creation seems to vie for preeminence here. Their roots coil and entwine deep within the vast earth;
their summits brush the Great Void, soaring and standing tall in majestic isolation. Cascading springs flow on and off, white...

Clouds veil and reflect its splendor, unfolding a natural masterpiece of painting. Where city walls join and battlements line one another, emerald cliffs and vermilion crags display carvings as fine as autumn down;
even a master craftsman would set aside his brush, and a divine artisan would tuck away his chisel. In the past, I engaged in travels of pilgrimage, wandering through each of those places.
Layer upon layer, ridge upon ridge, it is a realm like the Flower Treasury World (*Avataṃsaka-dhātu*); every bamboo and every tree stands as a banner of adornment.
Mao: Suddenly, both mind and environment are stilled; one is unaware that there is no place for the dust of worldly toil to dwell.
Thirty years have passed since we last met—how swiftly the years have flowed on! My aged steps can no longer move, yet my spiritual perception remains ever keen.

I bid you farewell before you have even departed; with the spirit as my horse, I wheel my rump along. Seated firmly upon my rush mat and bamboo couch, it seems as if I hear [your voice] faintly by my ear.
Hearing the Sound of Pines and Waves.
A Song of Chu Clouds Presented to the Venerable Shangren Zhang.
The clouds over the River of Chu are like a canopy; The waves upon the waters of the River of Chu are like boiling broth. The river water flows eastward, day and night.

Busy! Even the clouds have no intentionality, yet they are naturally worthy of love. Starting from a mere span, they spread across the universe; rolling up and unfolding, appearing and disappearing, all is tranquil and at ease.
When the golden cock crows three times, the city of Ying awakens; the five colors of its patterns are how brilliantly variegated!

Nail it down and hang it high—thus does the National Teacher preserve his standard for ten thousand ages. It is not merely to provide rain that moistens the parched and withered; he casually twists it apart.
The horns of the azure dragon are snapped; for many years, the land of Chu has been filled with the dust of war. Who now is the man who sleeps amidst the clouds?
One by one, as I gently stroke them from the beginning, heaven opens and earth parts, returning the warmth of spring.
On my first birthday, I sent word to Jitong:
"On this day last year atop Mount Lingxiao, I encountered my first birthday with no one to notice me;

only you knew that I was born on this day, and specially prepared the kitchen to cook the noodle soup for me. On this day this year, to the east of the Eastern Sea, my single body drifts like [a leaf]."
Severing the weeds. In the transformations of destiny, there is success and failure, praise and blame. Years and days are no different from one another. On this very day last year, it ended here;
next year and the year after, they will not cease. Turning through the eons of subtle dust, it begins once again from the very start.
How many Mount Vipula mountains have been piled up in bones? How many oceans of milk have been drunk? They are not few. Those with horns...
Clad in fur, yet wearing precious robes; like flowers in the sky, shadows, mirages, and waves. My original non-arising has become a day of birth;
from its origin, there is no need to recognize father or mother. Even if you were to recognize him today, it would still be like eating salt to quench thirst.
The man of the Way named Mukan has a small world within his breast; he hollowed out wood to make a hermitage and dwells thus.

Having already settled the fundamental principles with a single mattock, what harm is there in looking at the tree again after ten kalpas? He has brushed aside the foul old woman of those days—what warmth is there in the three months of winter?

It is vast; though the kalpa-fire blazes fiercely, it cannot consume it. Before the cliffs, the white sun flies like a shuttle. At the base of the rooms and the tops of the gates, there is a most profound serenity.
Without hinges or bolts, they allow for coming and going at will. To store food, what need is there for walls of white jade? To display its name, why use a plaque of yellow gold?
At midnight, the frost-moon rests upon the branches of meditation; the dense leaves cast shadows over the azure lapis lazuli. Throughout the eight directions...
Luminous and clear, ten thousand sounds are hushed; a single expanse of pure light, neither waxing nor waning. The old man Zhaozhou did not know there was something beyond:
he simply gallops east and then rushes west. When one touches upon his "trap-for-tigers" mechanism, he raises his fist, aligned with the Big Dipper.
The attendant Tao pricked his own blood to transcribe the Lotus Sūtra, concealing its brilliance and obscuring his traces;
yet he could not avoid lingering in the midst of the mundane or stagnating in empty stillness. To encounter the essential function face-to-face and realize the One Vehicle—this is the true path.
It appears this too is the power of skillful means. The assembly on Vulture Peak is eternally majestic; why need one manifest the ultimate to reveal the provisional?
That Śākyamuni did not receive a prediction from Dīpaṃkara is but a baseless legend.

With the blood of her own birth dripping from the tips of her fingers, her broad and long tongue shines like a radiant red lotus. She drags one out from the eighty thousand gates of worldly toil, seizing directly by the heart and liver.
Casting raw iron: do you not see Yan Fahu, who flits about eating and drinking in the houses of butchers and wine-sellers?
Amidst the burning house, he sports at will, laughing at those outside the gate who seek the three vehicles.
Song of the Resting Hermitage The Venerable Tang requested that I sing of De Shan’s departure for the South. How magnificent was his expansion of this Way!

For a thousand years, the monastic communities have cherished his legacy, just as the people of Shao left behind the sweet-tasting *táng* trees. Throughout every land and every atom, he wanders at will; atop the solitary peak, he dwells for a while.
Rest awhile. The thatched hut is woven together, yet the eternal stream flows forth. Buddhas and patriarchs crowd together, listening to scoldings and rebukes.

To wander and to rest is no ordinary matter; striking east and west, one opens the profound gate. Let the vegetable leaves drift with the flowing water; the white clouds still nestle upon the green mountains.
Alone, I close the wooden door as all worldly affairs cease; my staff and straw sandals hang upon the high wall. At the bottom of the mountain stream...
The hidden dragon cannot endure sleep; last night, a thunderclap struck before the eaves.
The song of the ancient sword is for the pleasure of the Abbot;
he composes on "Yin and Yang as Charcoal, Heaven and Earth as a Furnace. Feilian fans the bellows and the primal breath exhales; all things are smelted and refined until not even a trace remains.

The dross is cast off; the divine sword emerges from its mold in an instant. One can imagine the place where it was first forged: gods and spirits wailed in grief, and *chi-mei* demons fled in terror.

Transmitted through the seven Buddhas down to the present day, its blade remains brilliantly lustrous and ever-sharper. In the past, Mañjuśrī used it most intimately, casually brandishing it toward the body of the Tathāgata.
Its tiger-like energy surges with light, piercing the Ox and Dipper constellations; the dragon’s form leaps forth.
The waters are clear and free of dust. In what year did the handle and pommel fall into your hands? With a single strike facing the sun, the bronze bell roars;
sitting and cutting off heaven and earth, you establish Great Peace. With bristling hair and disheveled locks, who dares to follow behind?
The Radiant Chamber was built for Master Tianyuan of the Two Holy Heavens;
its brilliance surpasses all things past and present. Even the *cakṣur-vijñāna* (the eye of Śakra) finds it difficult to behold. Where there is no radiance, it manifests radiance;
where there are no doors or gates, it opens doors and gates. Therefore, the radiance is immeasurable, and the doors and gates are vast and open.
The borderlands: the closer one draws to them, the further away they become. Toying with the shadows and lights of others brings no auspiciousness. A man of the Way should keep himself pure and bare;
even if light and darkness are both forgotten, he must still be struck. Though Longtan was skilled at maintaining [the Dharma], extinguishing a paper lamp became a source of censure.
When the sparse curtains are rolled up, the spring day is long; the myriad phenomena are revealed, impossible to conceal. When a guest arrives—
When asked, there is no leisure to answer; with a smile, he points to the azure mountains beyond the lake.
With the great staff of non-self, he strikes at empty space; yet empty space has never felt pain. With foul words, he reviles a wooden man; yet the wooden man has never felt anger.

If one asks how this can be so, it is because of the absence of self (*anātman*). Where there is no self, all things are non-existent. Phenomena (*dharma*) revolve and intermingle with one another of their own accord:
when the boat moves, the bank must shift; when the boat stays still, the bank remains still. By striking the fire and seeking a bubble, one thoroughly perceives the meaning of non-self.
Seeing Han Zangzhu Return to Shushan (His Style Name:
Zhaohui) The wooden snake of Shushan wears horns upon its head; A forest of murderous energy fills the vast expanse. The Master himself once took it up and played with it;

That he did not suffer from its venomous mouth is itself a masterpiece. Sometimes it slumbers in concealment within the Vairocana-realm; Even the Ten Sages and Three Worthies find it difficult to reach.
Approaching closely, he suddenly leaps forth, displaying his heroic majesty; from level ground, he rolls up waves a thousand fathoms high. "Go back!
Go back!"—the Buddha-sun of the Awakened Heaven shines once more with brilliance. I ask you, my short uncle: with whom do you hold hands as you ascend the high terrace?
I present these scissors and tweezers to Yusheng;
Yusheng, listen to my Way. Which patch-robed monk lacks a head? His nostrils have always hung downward.
When you cannot find them, stop seeking elsewhere. Yusheng, Yusheng, remember my words: with the golden blades in hand, it is appropriate [to act].
Earnest and sincere. When one forgets both the adverse and the favorable, this is the Way. When the veins and arteries are not revealed, one is a true immortal.
Take heed of my words and listen to my teaching: all is merely following others in rising and falling at will. It is better to sweep away the weeds of ignorance with total sincerity.

Perfectly round and bright, shining clearly, it is free from all finicky distinctions and unites the ugly with the beautiful. With a single snap of the fingers, the heavens and seas are vast; ten billion [worlds...]
Mount Sumeru is small within the eye;
Tan Weina has composed verses in response to the rhymes of two venerable elders from the Eastern Region of Gulin.
The tiger’s fangs and claws at Huqiu are fierce; my narrow vision has long idly sketched its likeness. Its majestic wind howls through the forests;
its murderous aura is dense as it wears horns upon its head. The phoenix of Fengtai possesses nine-fold plumage; after five hundred years, it encounters this work.
Upon the Aru Pavilion of Qiyang, it cries out but once; the sagely virtue and illustrious conduct are suddenly illuminated. Alas! My life—
Thereafter, he regretted not having held the whip to follow him. He still longs for those lofty discourses where droplets of saliva fell;

Master Shijie and Chan Master Juedou were truly fierce and sharp. They did not cling to either the state of "awakened clarity" (*xingxing*) or "unconsciousness" (*wuji*), yet they manifested two distinct aspects through their powerful differentiation.
Set aside! To miss the meaning of the Western-coming Patriarch is like letting go of the rabbit while chasing the hawk; to say "mind is Buddha" is like seeking a stem from a flower in the sky;

to say "neither mind nor object" is likewise seeking a stem from a flower in the sky. Turn yourself around at the head of the hundred grasses and leap out of the field of the primordial kalpa. At midnight, there is perfect clarity.
At daybreak, nothing is revealed; the wheel of the sun pushes forth from the eastern gate of the sea. The golden crow tramples the coral trees.

The Peak of the Sun sings for the sake of the layman Sheng, as Xihe whips the sun upward to Mount Fusang. The lingering stars and the morning moon both flee and hide; the high peak emerging from the sea is the very first.

Illumination. Grasses and trees shimmer as golden light floats upon them. In a surge of inspiration, I shake out my robes and ascend the highest peak. Looking down upon the human world, it is like a pit or a well.
Breathing in the primal qi, my mind and spirit merge in harmony. Casting off worldly toil, I give rise to profound reflection. In the realm of the One True, there is neither difference nor sameness.
The Śrāvakas are like those intoxicated by wine, as if mute and deaf. How can I find that aged man of many ailments from Vaiśālī to grasp [the truth] with him?
Clapping his hands in rhythm, he sang of Mount Ilbong:

"Mount Tebong stands alone, a solitary peak towering between heaven and earth. One cannot reach it by looking upward; one can only toil in climbing. I know who dwells in this place of utter seclusion."
Summit. Vegetable leaves flow out into the clear, winding stream; mists roll up and smoke unfurls as the sun undergoes a thousand transformations.
Before the withered trees on the mountain crags, the path winds and turns; when Sudhana arrived here, he too hesitated. Where can one personally receive the grace of the Master’s countenance?
Flowers bloom and fall as spring follows autumn. Even Mount Tai is not enough to be a companion. On the back of the rock, beneath the shade of ivy, deer lie down; before the wind, the sun—
Below, the *lìliú* [cuckoo] cries out; a thousand wonders and ten thousand marvels cannot be fully described. Having attained the essential meaning, one forgets words and the mind understands itself.
Old Yangqi plows his fields to earn his rice; it is said that in recent years he has composed verses on returning to seclusion.
The snow-capped crags are towering and steep, a single slab of stone. It shines and gleams like a mountain of silver; though worldly people may gaze upon it from afar, they cannot reach it.
As one contemplates it, the hair on one's skin and the bones of one's marrow feel cold. To the very end, no idle grasses or trees grow there; the six-flaked blossoms fall in profusion.
In continuous succession, the great drought parches the earth and shimmering mirages float; a single kind of coolness is naturally sufficient.

In what year was the bright moon’s wheel cast down? It is transparent through and through, without a speck of dust. Do not dig open the caverns of primordial chaos; otherwise, you will vainly remain clinging to the source from which you came.
While traveling along the road, a practitioner requested a verse;
my luggage was already outside the gate. He urged me to hurry onto the path, waiting with his feet tapping. The Zen man sought a verse as urgently as a bowstring.
Shaking out my heart and mind, I found nothing to write. Fortunately, there is a ready-made secret method; I shall give it to him directly and clearly.
He said: "Vairocana is the Lord of the Dharmakāya; what are Śākyamuni, Maitreya, Mañjuśrī, and Samantabhadra? They are nothing but dried excrement sticks.
Without stirring so much as a speck of dust, one attains direct realization; ten thousand miles and a thousand leagues are swept away in a single stroke. Pshaw! Pshaw! Pshaw!"
To the Zen practitioner Mi, I show the patriarchs’ secret intent: it is utterly beyond words and speech; it is right here, right now. To attempt to grasp it is to miss it.
Have you not seen how Layman Lu pursued Master Ming all the way to the summit of Mount Dayu, where he was awakened by the instruction, "Do not think of good or evil"?
He then inquired further, saying, "Beyond these aforementioned secret words and secret meanings, is there yet another secret?
The Master then said to him, "If you were to turn back and reflect upon your own original face, the secret would reside right within you.
To speak in such a manner is already to point to a deer and call it a horse, or to call six a three; how much more so to gallop east and west, asking about Chan and asking about [the teachings]?

The Way: all day long one chatters, yet not a single mechanism is revealed; though one has a mouth, it is like a pair of tongs. The foolish are naturally oblivious, while the wise understand one another.
*Tu!* If you are a truly authentic patch-robed monk, you would rather freeze to death or starve to death than ever put on that "hawk-stink" robe.
Master Cangzhu returns to True Suchness;

his original spirit was already present when he lived and vanished when he departed. He pulled out the nostrils—just so! The myriad phenomena, dense and vast, are startled and stick out their tongues.

A white ox stands in the open field, radiating a cold light; not a single speck of dust remains within the realm of True Suchness (*tathatā*). The jade palace and pearl pavilions are most elegant and refined;
the "broken sand bowl" passed down through three generations is struck and tapped haphazardly to demand a high price.
It cannot be contained within the entire Tripitaka; it lies in wild disarray at the tips of the hundred grasses. Suddenly, a *maṇi* jewel is cast forth—red, white, blue, and yellow.
Following the five colors, the Master’s two eyes are as clear as mirrors; the great trichiliocosm is transparently penetrated without remainder.
Awaiting your return to pluck the tiger’s whiskers, you shall surely reverse the commands of Makara.

Seeing Zhu Xian depart for Jiuxian Temple, I sigh that the strings of Shaolin have snapped with no glue to mend them. A unicorn’s horn or a phoenix’s beak is hard to find in this world; fortunately, there is this man whose intellectual power is strong.
He wishes to twist tortoise hair into new strings—tortoise hair strings are most extraordinary; once played, they will move the multitudes of the human realm.
The sound has ceased. Though gold may not be cast into bells, Ziziqi could still discern them; when the notes of Gong and Shang are confused, who is there to distinguish them?
The Nine Immortals, graceful and transcending the mundane, have come on wind-chariots and cloud-borne carriages to seek you out. As you depart, do not linger.

Since you have elder masters to assist and guide you, surely there will be local lords to provide external protection. You must leave a legacy for future generations and avoid bringing shame upon the sages of the past.
I, an old man, know no way to accompany you; for your sake, I shall wash my ears at the head of the Eastern Sea. For your sake, I shall wash my ears at the head of the Eastern Sea.
Presented to Secretary Xun of Xuedou.

Before Huanglong emerged from Letan, he claimed his spirit swallowed the entire universe; yet when he came to see Ciming, he was unable to utter a word, and the pressure forced sweat from his forehead.
That yellow bitter gourd is not the ultimate bitterness; once medicinal mercury enters the forge, it flows away. How could Yunfeng’s words be mere idle talk?
Dongshan’s staff was merely a display of his skillful hand; as for the old woman of Tiantai— [The text ends here.]
Exaggerated rhetoric must be utterly defeated all at once before one may swallow its essence and grant oneself permission to speak. O practitioners of the Way, the Peak of Milk is not like that;

it establishes heaven and earth beyond measure and distinguishes guest and host amidst the dust. Whether you know or not that the fundamental principles of the school have fallen to the ground—on this day, who can rely upon to raise them up again?
Song of the Woodcutter Cloud, written for Yan Xisheng:
The old woodcutter of Xinzhou has eyes as clear as azure; A great axe at his waist, its edge bright with frost. He thrusts his body into the midst of heaped-up clouds;
He clears away the dense forest without expending effort. To require no effort is truly pitiable; The clouds deepen, the path turns, yet the firewood remains.
Shoulders! You laugh to death the seven hundred followers of Huangmei; when the sun has risen three *zhang*, they still sleep soundly.

Sometimes he lets out a single whistle—white clouds have no ears, yet they can still hear. Sometimes he sings a song—a single note joins the sound of the pines and winds as the clouds follow in pursuit.
Who can tell this to the man of Lanke? It would be well to smash his idle chessboard to pieces.
The Song of No Words was composed by the Elder Zhenru.
He sings of no words; the Way of no words is difficult to transmit through speech. To grasp it before the pivot of action is still to be a dull-witted man.
To understand through intellectual interpretation after the words are spoken is in vain. I originally possess a mouth, yet I have no tongue; when inspiration arises, I cannot help but sing a verse.
Beyond the Seven Golden Mountains, I seek one who understands; this has drawn forth the laughter of empty space until its sound chokes.

Have you not seen Śūnyatā-janman sitting in silent seclusion among the crags, while heavenly flowers fall in profusion across the earth? And have you not seen the sick man of Vaiśālī bestow [his teaching]?
One silence. The decrepit Mañjuśrī sighs that he can do nothing more. The two sturdy gates are both flung wide open; amidst the bright sun and blue sky, a thunderclap resounds.
*Ai yu xi!* Who knows this? Deep within the emerald stream, purple *zhī* fungi abound; cluster upon cluster, shimmering and radiant, they are enough to stave off hunger.
Blocking the idle chatter of all quarters, he takes up his iron flute and blows it in wild, chaotic strains.
To the attendant Quan:
Radiant and luminous, swirling and surging within the great void, surging eastward and submerging westward. Under the skin of Yuanwu there is blood;
on the tongue of the Fifth Patriarch there is no bone. He restrains the spirited stallion that would bolt, and releases the magnificent falcon soaring through the vast heavens.
At one moment, the opportunity before one’s eyes is lost; the golden rooster flaps its wings as the balustrade bends.

He laughs at those who, having no cause for it, disturb the spring heart, repeatedly calling for "Little Jade" on behalf of the patron. Whether joyful or not, whether sufficient or not, six times six remains thirty-six.
A Gift to Daoist Master Lingyunfeng (The character "Dao" was assigned for this verse).
Sitting through the summer retreat without leaving my door, the dust of worldly ties has been swept clean. A feathered guest from Taoci Stream has come to visit me on the path of non-arising.
The Unborn cannot be learned; to attempt to learn it leads only to agitation. There is a Reality prior to Heaven and Earth, dark and profoundly remote.

The realms of the Immortal and the mundane are fundamentally one; awakening to this should be sought early. How could those like Zhi and Qiao have lived long? Yet Yan Hui and Ran Geng never met with untimely death.

The southern breeze dispels the scorching heat; deep green foliage and the songs of orioles mark the end of spring. With you, we both forget words; this dusty world is itself the Penglai isle. To Zongji Xingjue:
If you wish to practice Chan, practice it upon your own self. If you wish to study the classics to clarify the principles of nature, know that these principles are no different from your own self.
O kinsmen, do not distinguish between self and other within this. Those deluded by people wallow in the margins of words; it is just like a wick and oil being boiled together in a cauldron.
If you do not comprehend the source and its course beyond words, when will you bathe in the clear, cold abyss? I am old and have grown addicted to indolence;
until death there is no medicine to cure it. You are now in the prime of youth; day and night you ought to be diligent. Strike it, and you shall hit it.

From this day forward, even if I were to teach you and you were to scold me, you would know it is all in vain. Have you not seen how Guling, after traveling everywhere to seek instruction, attained this essential meaning and returned to explain its underlying principle to his own teacher?
Although I am not Guling’s teacher, I nonetheless hope that you will ultimately achieve solitary liberation and independence.
I show you, Preceptor Nian, how a fierce tiger kills a stone rabbit. Last night at the third watch, it suddenly came to life; now it sits crouched at the Stone Gate Pass.
To anyone who comes, it shall cut off their very life-force. As the old monk approaches to look closely, its fangs are like the edge of a sword and its claws...
It is like iron; one must know the essential points when directing it toward the various directions. It does not depend on others to stroke it in the direction of the hair.
I present this to the physiognomist Yuan Tingyu:
my form is formless, yet it possesses all forms; my body is bodiless, yet it manifests infinite bodies. This is the clarity of Li Lou.

None are able to discern it. How could the wisdom of Tang Ju be consulted? Were it not for that which transcends the vastness of physical form, how could one easily probe its true essence through ordinary means?
There is a scholar from Siming whose pupils are lacquered black; he has seen so many people pass before his eyes that he knows their fortunes and failures.
He does not mirror the face but mirrors the heart; in pointing out merits and faults, he is like one dispelling the ignorance of a child. Yesterday he came to me atop the pine crags, and...
Seeing that there are no words, the mind understands itself; fortune, misfortune, regret, and gain—discuss them all as finished. For now, let us strike the ice to brew mountain tea.
I urge you, Attendant Zhe:
before I had seen Guiyuan, there was nowhere for the Way of Chan to be applied; but after seeing Guiyuan, not a single word was used.
Where there is no place for application, application is most intimate. Therefore, I have humbly received the transmission from that master. It is not that there is a private lineage of transmission;

rather, one rolls right into the thicket of complications, exhausting the mouth and wearying the lips. Have you not seen how the Patriarch Yuanwu ate nothing but yellow myrobalan without knowing its bitterness?
Within the voice of the little jade girl, he found the path home, and from then on, Dongshan expanded the gate of his school. I—
Since there is nothing that can be said, you likewise have nothing to record. This paper-garment is fortunately as white as frost;
take care not to lightly soil it with dust and ink. Alas! The wind and moon of Shaolin are vast and boundless; a snapped string must be mended with phoenix-glue.
The Chapter on Not Returning: Yesterday he did not return; today he has not returned either. Since he does not return, I am left to sigh deeply in weariness.
For what reason do I sigh? Out of pity for this son who has lost his home; he has cast aside the ancestral estate to seek a livelihood abroad.

The years pass with little joy; they are like the lingering ripples upon the water. Since the source of the mind has not yet been made clear and vast, how can one endure this cycle of birth and death?

*Guilai Pian* (The Return Home): Return! Return! Return! By returning, one escapes the need for worldly entanglements. The taste of mountain springs is like sweet nectar; A seat of grass is a golden terrace.

In life, one should be self-sufficient; self-sufficiency is true heavenly fortune. It is better to sing the song of those who beat the earthen blocks than to weep at the end of one's wretched journey.
When not a single dharma lingers in the mind, the green mountains remain green through all four seasons. One breaks off pines and sits by the rocks, walking amidst white clouds beyond the forest.
The Begging Song, composed for Master Yuanshu by the Five-Peak Recluse Cimuwei:
When hunger comes, I go to the village ahead to beg for alms. My patched robe is disheveled like that of a quail;
my hair is matted and bristling like a hedgehog. When I get rice, I eat it immediately; when I get a drink, I swallow it at once. [I] stuff [my belly] full...
When the hungry belly is sated, one simply rests; who can speak of the flavor within this? Since my birth, I have possessed this bowl;
its inexhaustible enjoyment is truly a source of joy. It is neither copper, nor iron, nor gold; it is peerless and beyond compare, most wondrous and sublime.
Neither polished nor scraped clean, it is perfectly round and radiantly brilliant. At times I cast it toward the crossroads, utterly without regard for its value;
at other times I tuck it away within my bag of a hundred patches, enclosing it in layer upon layer.
When bystanders question me regarding its origins, I shout a single "Tsk! right in their faces. I laugh at old Śākyamuni, who spent his days begging for alms.

Restricting it to only seven households, I laugh at Vimalakīrti for relying on alms-begging and toiling to reach the Fragrant Accumulation (Gandhavyūha) realm. Who knows that I am not like this at all?
I roam at ease, moving according to my natural course like an immortal. Whomever I encounter is a donor; wherever I step out the door, I meet with the smoke of cooking fires.
A-he-he! Do you understand? The three realms are in turmoil, like flowers in the sky. To discuss the profound and speak of the wondrous—what is there to say?
Like rice and hemp stalks, the slightest movement brings about confusion and error. "Alas, alas! Listen to my vow: you must be careful not to clamor.
I shall never abandon you throughout birth and death; do not you, in turn, abandon me to seek a livelihood elsewhere."
To show the first opportunity of Master Shimo and his final word: to accept [the teaching] as soon as the mouth opens is already to fall into the secondary.
Have you not seen how Aṅgulimāla called out to the World-Honored One, "Stop! Stop!"? The World-Honored One said to him, "I have already stopped; it is you who have not."

It does not abide. This old man who looks on has, in his ordinary way, revealed it: like rolling a round stone from the crest of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, leaping down until one reaches level ground;
yet even that is not its place of rest. If Bodhidharma had not come from the East, [this would have been so].
The Second Patriarch did not go west; with gnarled and jagged teeth, he passed his time. Vast and indistinct, like the sands of the Ganges—this I give as a gift to Master Ne while I am ill.
My illness is truly beyond remedy; my hundred limbs feel as if struck by blows. You have come to seek a Chan verse; upon this thought, may you attain liberation.

I take up my brush and write this: the myriad phenomena respond in accord with the "Amen. The ocean of concealment cuts off even the slightest current; the azure dragon bares its head and horns. In the blue sky, thunder and lightning crash;

in the bright day, snow and hail fly. Have you not seen? When the total mechanism is severed in stillness, what need is there to speak of the demon of darkness, the demon of death, or the demon of affliction?
When a single thought is perfectly integrated, one suddenly transcends the stages of Equal Enlightenment and Sublime Enlightenment to reach the Unsurpassed.
Jue. Record of the Sayings of Chan Master Shu Zhong, Volume Four;
Record of the Sayings of Chan Master Shu Zhong, Volume Five.
Compiled by the student-monks Qing Sui and others,
these verses were sent to Master Yongzhang of Zhongzhu for his second visit.
Before the Guizi Hall stands an immortal of a thousand years; sighing, he stirs the six realms to produce thunder and wind. The first patriarch arrived from India during the Putong era;

upon meeting him by chance, his passions and consciousness were emptied. Demons and heretics were cowed and subdued to serve as attendants. Roaming freely amidst the mountains and waters of the two Zhejiang provinces, he lingered in this profound domain like the Vulture Peak.
Choosing this auspicious site, he cleared the ground to establish a Buddhist monastery; in the lofty hall, drums were beaten.

The sound of the drum rolls on and on. The fourfold assembly gathers like a dense forest. Glancing left and right with lotus-like eyes, they awaken to their respective natures, finding joy beyond the cage of worldly existence.
Your former incarnation was Baozhang; now you are this very Master. On the Stone of Three Lives, we once met. Young phoenixes and fine colts fill the world;
yet even a foal’s galloping stride must yield to the mighty stallion. You have personally entered the inner chamber to exhaust the beginning and the end. [He] circumambulates...

A hundred refinements do not turn base copper into gold; since our parting, your traces have been like drifting dandelion seeds. The new moon has appeared repeatedly, like a drawn bow; Ciming changed his robes and followed the wandering soldiers.
How could I dare forget my request for instruction? My heart remains devoted [to you]. The lingering embers of past incense offerings still exist;
where the incense smoke rises, a rainbow spans across. Alas! How profound is the occasion of meeting you! Do not let it pass like a flash of lightning or a spark from a flint.
In haste! Raising the whisk, he bows deeply. Having let out a shout, both ears must surely go deaf.
In the year Wushen, while sitting out the summer retreat at Jinge, I read the *Luohu Yalu* during my leisure from meditation.
Within it is recorded a verse by Guo Guangying of Zhushan, composed for Master Hong of Tongsuanshan in Yingzhou, who was styled Gudubiao.
Four Verses. I have composed these following the high rhyme to show them to the Attendant Ji, the Attendant Lu, the Attendant Shi, and the Attendant Dugu Zhao.
A single ray of divine light penetrates the nine heavens; Nirvana and birth-and-death are not two dharmas.
What need is there to transcend the ten stages of the Three Vehicles? Look at the patriarchal masters of the world below;
they vie with one another to emerge from their concealment, exhausting every mechanism and displaying every artifice. It is just like lighting a fire to try and burn empty space.
Dugu Zhao, Dugu Zhao! For nine years he faced the wall until grass grew on his tongue; he regretted killing himself by opening his mouth at the start.
A single word lightly uttered startled Old Xiao. In the end, he was bested by Deshan, Linji, and the two prefectures of Zhao and Mu.
Where there is a path, they block it; where there is a bridge, they break it.
Dugu Zhao, Dugu Zhao! On the mossy wall above his bed hangs a tea ladle. As the light of day breaks and the sun rises, he sleeps soundly;
yet with a single cry from outside the window, his mother’s pancakes burn. Hanshan raises his bamboo broom; Changting unties his cloth bag.
I ask those of this age: do you understand? If you do not, then the Master of Five Willows was originally surnamed Tao.
Dugu Biaozhi, Dugu Biaozhi! A single flask and a single bowl—how desolate! Moving freely and spontaneously, he is beyond cultivation and realization;
neither transcending nor not transcending the holy and the mundane, he transcends by himself. On precipices and sheer cliffs, a mass of purple gold;
amidst azure mists and emerald fogs, a white jade tuft. He splits the great void into two pieces; the stone woman sews together hair from a tortoise.
Presented to my Dharma-nephew, the Librarian Zhuang:
The dragon spits fire from its candle, burning through the void; Everywhere, rivers and streams have run dry. Sages and divine monks are no more in this world;

Who shall overturn the celestial ladle to wash away the scorching heat? The sun rises high at my thatched gate, yet the bolt remains unfastened. How could it be for the sake of a single mouthful of life?
Lingering Sorrows. In the southern and northern villages, the green rice has withered; In the upper and lower fields, yellow dust flows. Suddenly, outside the bamboo grove, I hear a knocking:

"Nephew, why have you come to these forest ravines? He holds in his hand a scroll of yellow oil-paper; Its jade-like moisture and pearl-like luster reveal a new composition. As I unfold it and read it, my mind and eyes open wide; It is as if I were drinking a cup of nectar. The heart of this old man— Lingering Sorrows. In the southern and northern villages, the green rice has withered; In the upper and lower fields, yellow dust flows. Suddenly, outside the bamboo grove, I hear a knocking: "Nephew, why have you come to these forest ravines? He holds in his hand a scroll of yellow oil-paper;
Its jade-like moisture and pearl-like luster reveal a new composition. As I unfold it and read it, my mind and eyes open wide; It is as if I were drinking a cup of nectar. The heart of this old man—
From this moment on, there is sudden awakening and clarity. In these final times, do not fear the collapse of the fundamental principles. I have a single phrase you must listen to:
do not rashly bring it forth before those lacking wisdom. The stone tiger in front of the mountain bites the rabbit; Tsa-sha hunts the nine-tailed beast.
When Master Daochu composed this lamentary verse, people said that Zhenji had died;
I say that Zhenji has been born. Zhenji is fundamentally not an illusion; it is because of illusory birth that the name "Zhenji" exists.

The moon is cold in the Zen quarters at night; the stone pagoda resounds with the spring rain. The very threads of the school’s fundamental principles are falling apart; I stand waiting, harboring nothing but lingering emotion. Later generations have lost their models;
those who lead and proclaim now turn their backs on the essential meaning. Having never attained the initial entry, they already claim to have ascended to the rank of the Patriarchs.
With power he reveals the upward-turning pivot, seeking to have them know their fundamental basis. One night, a Vairambha wind blew down the cool-shaded tree;

the Dragon River has many offspring, and the patterns are those of the phoenixes of the Vermilion Mountain. Gloriously illuminating the human and celestial realms, who in ancient or modern times could share in this?
Truly, your wisdom and power are strong; you uphold and control the teachings of the patriarchs and Buddhas. You cast forth the final word, a seamless, undivided whole.
Before the era of Wei-yin there was no "patriarch," and Bodhidharma was not my teacher. True emptiness is fundamentally equal; the three periods of time are but one single moment.

In a single kṣaṇa, immeasurable kalpas pass; even a flash of lightning seems slow by comparison. A physical life of fifty years is but a brief span, yet the reputation of one who has left home knows no end.

The ancients who showed the path of quiescence left home for the sake of birth and death; those who leave home today do not do so for that reason. Since birth and death have existed from the beginning, they are simply inexhaustible.

How much more so when one acts like an ordinary worldly person—neither treating friends as friends nor teachers as teachers? Thus they roam in vast crowds, habituating themselves to the vulgar and base;
at every turn they face a wall of ignorance. Why wait until another year to finally know shame? Since you have already become my disciples, you must daily redouble your efforts in conduct.
You must diligently investigate and penetrate the essence of the Chan school, the core intent of the teachings. [Morning worship before] sacred images...
Be diligent in your prostrations even during the night watches. Should you ever manage to enter the gate [of realization], your pure reputation will surely spread to the ears of others.
Be careful not to let time slip away in indolence; do not remain submerged headfirst in the stagnant water of death. I am now old and infirm, capable of nothing;
I shall simply dwell at ease in the mountains and forests as circumstances allow. When you come to inquire after me, I join my palms in greeting; face-to-face, how could I ever fail you?
Zhonggui of the Zhen family inscribed the name "Pure and White Abode" (Qingbai Ju) upon his dwelling.
The Daoist sits in meditation within this Pure and White Abode; body and mind unmoving, forever abiding in suchness (*tathatā*).

Deep in the lunar cavern hides the snow-lion; within the ice-clear pitcher rests the silver hare. Its colorless, pure, and true essence is wondrous and unfathomable; how could those of inferior or middling capacity ever reach it?
In that realm, one does not cultivate the practices of Brahma; how could one who serves the King of Emptiness be a house-thief guarding perverse meditation?
Transcendent and vast, encompassing the void, whether three feet or sixteen feet tall, they walk hand-in-hand home. This very person is the one whose elegance pierces to the bone.
Day and night, the six gates radiate brilliance. Among the sagely and sharp monks nowadays, those are few; often they seek from the outside. Fundamentally, there is nothing.
The stages are level and smooth; reaching this point, one must surely first trip and fall. O practitioners, O practitioners, listen to my words:
applying red and smearing green is known to be in vain. You must strip away everything at the critical moment; do not let yourselves fall into the realm of mere purity.
Let us count the ancient sages from the beginning with you: the style of Linji is most transcendent. He flung open the doors and windows to distinguish dragons from snakes;
earth split and heaven collapsed in a single shout.

A Morning Verse Presented to Attendant Zhe My school is vast and expansive like empty space; The boundless Dharma-realm is entirely contained within it. It is like a sage ruler receiving the myriad nations at court:
The wind follows the tiger, and the clouds follow the dragon. The source of the school has no source, and I have no self; Like the "White Snow" and "Yangchun," may you join in harmony.

Rarely have they come. Since the time of Caoqi, the transmission has been erroneous; the five schools branched out and became mere idle talk. Sitting in the thatched hall by day, one feels the coolness of the southern breeze;
after the rain, the plants and trees waft a celestial fragrance. The news of the ultimate source is simply this;
there is nothing else extraordinary to discuss.
I present this to my esteemed friend from Fujian, who aspires to be a person of the Supreme Vehicle (Agrayāna). You must, directly and immediately, realize your true nature (*dharmatā*).

If you indeed perceive it with clarity, then naturally your head will be upright and your tail straight; all myriad concerns will be stilled, and the four maladies will be severed. You will be like a Dragon Spring sword drawn from its scabbard, appearing when needed.

A bright mirror upon a stand: those who look ahead and glance behind mistake the reflection for the head and lose sight of their own. Those who dodge blades and hide behind sharp points forfeit their bodies and lives.
Xuan Sha was merely this old fisherman; he carried his burden on one shoulder with nothing left over.
Presented to Venerable Wù as Head of the Monks:
The ultimate true sound—upon whom shall it rely for continuation? Short dances and long songs are but empty toil. To receive echoes and grasp at shadows is to speak in vain;
When rhythm and beat coincide, one "unicorn" suffices. The wedge drives out the wedge, the mechanism seizes the mechanism; Sweeping away the paths of thought, one transcends.
Profound and subtle! The horned clay ox enters the sea and bellows; the featherless iron hawk soars on the wind.

In the field of Dharma-battle, Old Xinghua captures the living and seizes the active, striking fear into all. Kebin’s expulsion from the monastery was a moment of glory—how many can truly manage to slip out and enter within?
A gift for Attendant Quan:
In relying on a teacher and seeking friends, one must be careful in one’s selection. To have a superior friend and an excellent teacher is the best strategy.

One who is like a chronic ailment must encounter medicine that brings relief; one who is like a withered sprout must encounter the sweet rain. For this reason, I sent the administrative officer to visit Niaoke and Xuefeng.
Feng attained realization under Lao Nuo; fortunately, he possessed the standard of the ancestral predecessors, which can naturally serve as a model and a paradigm.
At twilight, one rubs the forehead while gazing toward the rising sun; with a single crow from the golden cock, all under heaven becomes bright.

A Song for the Hermitage on White Cloud Mountain, Presented to the Abbot Lin The white clouds drift and vanish, leaving no trace; They seem to have a private pact with the green mountains alone. In the evening they fly above the mountain peaks;
At dawn they again sweep across its base. The man of the Way dwells in emptiness and stillness; He takes no pleasure in worldly fame. Since he loves...

The white clouds are white; moreover, he delights in the green of the blue mountains. Having built this thatched cottage for deep seclusion, he points with a smile to the clouds and mountains as his courtyard.
The clouds and mountains are, in truth, my own nature; my nature is fundamentally the spiritual essence of the clouds and mountains.
When cold, I wear the clouds as a robe; when hungry, I drink the green of the mountains. In daily life, I am carefree and never lacking; even a Buddha has never wished to be such as this.
That consciousness perceives the honors and humiliations of the human world.

I send the attendant Wei to visit his uncle, Master Yin-zong, to inquire after him—like the pines of Mount Cu-lai and the bamboo of the Wei River, with their sturdy joints and lofty standards rising above the mundane. The conduct and aspirations of a monk are likewise so.
Ah! To accept one’s lot in a secluded mountain, embracing solitude—when Xiangyan struck once, all that was known was forgotten.
When Niaoke sat cross-legged upon a precarious branch, he used only the pines and bamboos to preach the Dharma; what need was there for him to pick up and blow on a wisp of cloth?
The Master at Dongsi has a younger brother; do not neglect your affairs to run about in pursuit of fame. The iron boat has long since been launched; it is time to set sail home.
Ripening with the eastern breeze, I, an old man, am unable to accompany you; in seeing you off, my heart feels but a sense of deep anxiety. I say to you:
our Way is now truly desolate; upon whose shoulders shall this heavy burden of ten thousand *jin* rest?
The Abbot Zangxiu, formerly named Fangshi, later dreamed while attending a Chan banquet that he entered Weiyu Mountain and obtained a rare stone about an inch square,
upon whose surface was the inscription "Zongyin" (Seal of the Lineage). He subsequently changed his former name to Zongyin and requested a verse.
The Chan master dreamed he entered Mount Weiyu; his coughing and clearing of the throat repeatedly opened the gates of the clouds.

Who sent the mountain spirit to present this extraordinary stone? Held in his hand, its color was not merely crimson. The inscription of the patriarchal seal appeared with brilliant clarity; when he raised it up, thousands and tens of thousands beheld it.
At that moment, the mandate was carried out throughout Wu and Yue; East Land and West Heaven were seen to be level and expansive. Upon waking, he lay back in repose.
Sleeping upon my bed, I reflect on the past with a sense of vast bewilderment. The Tathāgatas of the three periods all spoke of it as a dream;

now there remain only the provisional and the ultimate, the partial and the perfect. Renaming and changing words—all rests within me; appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unfolding, nothing is not permissible.
If someone further asks about the "Iron Ox" mechanism, I pick up my black staff and strike them right on the head.
The servant Chen Anshou of Ruiyan requests the Dharma: fundamentally, there is no high or low.
It is only the ignorant who give rise to discrimination. Following conditions and conforming to types, forms are assigned;
it is just like the bright moon in the sky—how could it be superior for appearing in clear water? How could it be inferior for reflecting in a dirty stream? Its coming and going have no fixed time.
Functioning without deficiency, Ruiyan repeatedly calls out, "O Master!"—and he does not do so outside of this very moment. *Du!* Dagu presents his *tong* staff to the Abbot Zangchu:
"Dagu is warm like a secret flame;
as soon as it is subjected to carving and polishing, flaws and blemishes arise. One must know that for the third offering, it does not come from itself."
Rare! To have it all returned is already a missed opportunity. Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the universe, even a city-sized gem is difficult to repay with its full value.
When the dark moon hides, the bright moon appears; how could it be like a dull stone buried in a desolate mountain?

Having personally recovered it from within the Tathāgata-garbha, its wealth and glory pervade the heavens without rival. Only another who can discern jewels—the blue-eyed barbarian—can truly recognize it. To treat this as a mere trifle would be reckless.
How could they possibly understand?
Regarding the gift of practicing Chan for the Abbot He:
practice Chan! Practice Chan! One who practices Chan must be a true man of great resolve; one should believe that practicing Chan is the most straightforward way to settle all affairs.
Simply hold up Zhaozhou’s “No. Walk and you hold it; sit and you hold it. Constantly maintain this mindfulness throughout walking, standing, sitting, and lying down.
Suddenly, when the black lacquer bucket is smashed, you will stand shoulder to shoulder with all the sages.

Thus, Lǎnzàn did not accept the imperial edict on yellow hemp, and Fúróng did not accept the purple cassock. Since one has already studied Chan to transcend birth and death, who would be willing to follow after [worldly honors]?
Things have become self-deception. The Chan practice of recent times is not at all [authentic]. Everyone has abandoned the true teacher to merely study words;

even if they manage to master such speech, it is just like raising a parrot in an ornate cage. The parrot follows people with its cleverly modulated tongue, speaking a thousand and ten thousand ways throughout the day.
If you ask what the matter of its speech is, it speaks immediately upon being questioned—how can one discern anything?
I urge those born later to be fierce and resolute; when it touches the palm of your hand, you must instantly perceive it. The scriptures of the Three Vehicles are like sand within rice;
the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are but specks in the eye. To practice Chan—oh, to practice Chan! A single thread of thought is no sound strategy.
How admirable is the immortal Zhang Guolao! He truly had no use for his medicinal gourd.

This verse on the Nature School (Xingzong) shown to Chan Master Han demonstrates that the true nature is as vast as empty space; standing alone and precarious, he established the school. To deliberate upon existence and non-existence is like probing the waters.
The moon; setting forth discourse on good and evil, it is judged by the wind of heaven. I do not know whose eyebrows he speaks of. Let me ask: what season is it now?
True nature is like empty space, yet even this is but a provisional name. To cling to such names is the dullest of the dull.

This one school of ours is the most difficult to support. Deshan and Linji had skin as hard as leather; their staffs and shouts flew back and forth, shaking the world for ten thousand generations. How they soar, transcending all!
Whom can you hope to climb upon? "The younger generation is to be feared"—this is what the ancients said. Be careful not to wander aimlessly about;
a single word can destroy the kings of heterodox views, and only then will Shaoshi be able to truly comfort your heart.
Following the rhyme of the Southern Hall: Seeing off Chan Master Shou as he returns to Fusang.
The sound of iron horses at the head of the house rings out—*ding-dong*. Clear and distinct, they spread the true wind. This old man’s dreams have grown deep within the Penglai Palace;

The grand music of the celestial court fills his ears. Upon awakening, he realizes that in the carriage he has encountered the divine; The transcendent echoes and lingering tones compete in resonance.

Rushing and pouring forth—yet upon waking from the dream, there is never a mind of arising or ceasing. It is perfectly still, like a tuft of cotton soaked in mud. The practitioner pushes open the door while the dew is still wet;

looking at one another with a smile, it is not a matter of mere superficiality. Ten lifetimes of past and present merge within the present thought; the great trichiliocosm returns to the tip of a single hair.
I admire how, as you grow older in years, your hands and feet have become so agile, appearing and disappearing with a divine mechanism that sweeps like a flash of lightning. —Nantang.

Within the chamber, the morning falcon soars; the bowl-bag, weighing a thousand *qín*, has already been handed down. Recalling those days attending at the meditation seat, as soon as a word was uttered, one was met with a chest-trampling kick.
The *wǎngxiàng* grasps the bright pearl, leaving the mud and water behind; the mirror of Xuanyuan opens from its dusty casket.
I see you off at the banks of the Yin River in the morning; you shall travel far upon the eastward-bound vessel. I, an old man, shall close my door and continue my sleep;
I have no more strength of mind to discuss the single transmission.
Following the rhyme of Master Chushih, I present this to Attendant Zhi:
not using intention to dispel intention, nor using words to dispel words—sitting decisively at the very head, the bright sun hangs in the blue sky.
In the western chamber, we brothers have mouths too lazy to speak of Chan. With bamboo rakes wielded at random, we naturally forget the orthodox and the deviant.
Towering heights, we delve into the secret cave; with a roar, we cast aside the dark trap. We bring to death all living monks, so that they may directly shed their fetters.
You, Ziyuan and your peers, have both fully realized the legacy of teacher and disciple. You do not compete for superiority, but strive to match the shoulders of the ancients.
Like autumn hawks spreading their six feathers, we watch with bated breath as you soar alone. Flying across the nine heavens, the expanse of your mind empties the eight directions.
How can this be compared to a pig that rolls in its own dung? It is constantly confined within its pen; three times it calls, and three times it responds, for its secret intent lies with you.
Upon the eight precious rags of his robe, the thin places will surely be the first to wear through.
At the Xiyou Studio, for the sake of Elder Zhen, I write:
Take one more step from the top of the hundred-foot pole; the black-lacquered Kunlun is pointed out. Retreat one step from the top of the hundred-foot pole;
the heels have not yet trodden upon the path that reaches heaven. Advancing is not advancing, and retreating is not retreating; having leaped forth, one is already within the *muhūrta*.
Turning his back, advancing is retreating and retreating is advancing; with great compassion he holds the inverted seal of the Māra King.
It is laughable that old Zhaozhou of those days—where would one seek the gateway of such a master? The old woman of Mount Tai could not discern it;
she only knew how to look at the tower and then strike the tower. He has broken the iron staff he used all his life and cut off the idle delusions of all quarters. One room.
The vast emptiness opens throughout the day; since he has not come, I have not gone. After the rain, the sparse curtains are drawn up on their hooks;
white clouds flow like water across the edge of heaven. On Mount Boshan, incense smoke billows as the true nature (*dharmatā*) is discussed; outside the window, a yellow oriole calls out once.
In the same rhyme, I present this to the monk Yue Shang, while also addressing my uncle Mu’an:
"Who is foremost among the masters? He has surpassed the two, three, four, and seven [schools].
Striking the void to test the true adept—only Kaiyuan truly stands out. A fifth-generation descendant of Xiqiu, his name is lofty and his virtue is weighty; he is a true monk."
The Honored One of the Center, Maheśvara, has eyes upon his crown; from above, he gazes down upon the four seas as if they were cups and basins.

You, my son, possess a refined and noble character; be solemn and earnest in your reliance and study, and utterly avoid negligence. Within the chamber, he extended his hand to you, granting you a direct transmission—how could this be compared to wading through waves to grasp the bright moon?
Alas, in all matters I am inferior to others, yet toward your father, our hearts are uniquely close. Thus I speak to you.
Recently I have attained the Dharma of peace and happiness; when weariness comes, I simply rely upon my mat.
To the Zen practitioner seeking a long verse:
Lately, those who study Zen have taken a liking to long verses; as soon as they write a short one, they are displeased. Whether a phrase is long or short, the principle remains the same.
1. Why, within this, do we distinguish between "this" and "that"? The long does not know how long it is; the short does not know how short it is.
If one can directly investigate the source, both long and short arise from the deluded mind. A-he-he! La-la-li!
Taking Mount Sumeru as a brush and empty space as paper, I write out a single phrase to present for your journey. From here on, follow your own way.
Comparing long and short—do not let yourself lose what belongs to your own house.
Following the original rhyme to show Master Cāngzhǔ Yì:
"Not so, not so; thus it is, thus it is. As soon as one distinguishes between the Buddha-realm and the demon-palace, there are already those who claim my village as their own.
Mental attention explains horizontally; vertical explanation misses the mark. Direct pointing and single transmission—when seeing rice, everyone knows how to eat it;

yet drinking the poison-draught is permitted only to Cao Man. I, an old man dwelling in a hermitage, have become carefree and detached; the shackles at my wooden gate are untied, for I have no heart to be bound. "O seeker of the Way, from where do you come so early?
He holds his golden staff upside down and plants it right before one's face. Above the Buddhas and Patriarchs there is no mysterious barrier. Seven.

Pervading the eight directions and reaching the realm of rest, he guards the boundaries of seclusion. How could one not possess the hand of Lord Ren that casts his fishing line? With a single pull, he drags up the six giant tortoises and the three mountain-islands.

To the monk Shi-jian: the divine sword is held in your grasp; its cold radiance stands solitary. The chi-mei demons and the wang-liang shadows all flee in retreat. The practitioners of the Three Vehicles and the Ten Stages are summoned like maidservants.
A slave! The nostrils of the True Man of No-Rank are short; the eyebrows of the Youth of the Snowy Mountains are coarse.
Inscribed on the挽章 (挽章, elegies) for Master Ximing:
"The Qilin may be killed, the Phoenix may be cooked; the world cannot do without this master. The green pines may be carved, the cypresses may be cut."

Kao. The Confucian community cannot do without this old man. This old man’s mind is like the sun and moon suspended in the sky; it illuminates the obscure and shatters the darkness without partiality.
Previously, he came to the Southern Heaven wielding his axe, guiding the forces of creation with specialized mastery.

When the conditions for such mastery were not yet favorable, he leaned back on his desk in the deep mountains until willow trees grew from his elbows. Fully realizing that wealth and honor are like floating clouds, he daily recited the *Sūtra of Infinite Life*.
A hundred thousand mouths recite the name of Amitābha; heart-mind after heart-mind, every thought flows like a cascading river.
The mind of Amitābha is my own mind; my own mind has long since departed from Saṃsāra. How truly pitiable! How truly lamentable!
Do not discuss birth and death with the Master; birth and death have always been fundamentally empty and still.
The spontaneous cannot be sung;
that which can be sung is not spontaneous. Even the mouths of Mozi and Zhuangzi were unable to express it; though Wang Mai went beyond, his "Xiaoyao" chapter remains but empty words.
As for Laozi and Śākyamuni, when have they ever been free from the entanglements of the world? No sooner had they emerged from their mothers' wombs than they began to grasp at things.
Strange! Pointing his fingers at the earth and then pointing at the heavens, he wished to make known the Way of spontaneity:

"Do not seek it elsewhere. When autumn arrives, the thousand mountains shed their crimson leaves; when spring comes, green grass grows everywhere across the ground. All myriad creatures suddenly flourish, each nourishing itself and withering on its own.

Each and every thing accords with its season; each and every thing is perfectly wondrous. If one claims that a Creator causes them to be so, then the Creator ultimately becomes something possessing a mind.
If you insist that the Creator is fundamentally without mind, then if the Creator is mindless, who creates all things? A-he-he!
Lü Zhōngbīn, you should understand this well.
Huang Mengbin, styled as the Layman Wenen, requested a verse:
"If there is something heard that can be heard, it is not true hearing. How could true hearing be attained by means of hearing?

To seek to reach true hearing and exhaust the nature of hearing, do not employ conceptualization or deliberation to pass judgment. Even the word 'true' is a false statement; it is like trying to affix [a name] to empty space."
Ear Acupuncture. How laughable is the monkey that does not still its mind; in deluded madness, it seeks the bright moon at the bottom of the water.

When the Immortal of Poshan (Suzhou) traveled through Mount Lu in days of yore, he made one mistake of hearing that was no ordinary error. He pointed out that the sound of the brook is the broad and long tongue [of the Buddha];

to this day, this story remains difficult to exhaust. Master Huang, Master Huang, you are truly a master of the craft; as soon as you open your mouth, you let out the roar of a lion. Sound and form...
Rolling out from amidst the heap, he startles the Dharma-body as it hides within the Northern Dipper.
Layman Lu seeks a verse on non-concealment:
"Have you not seen? On Mount Lu there were once eighteen worthies; they opened a pond, formed a society, and together planted lotuses. They strove with all their might to investigate Zen..."

He has transcended birth and death; with uplifted sincerity and pure tranquility, he remains ever-vigilant. You now possess the aspiration to emulate the sages of old, so you have come specifically to seek instruction and request my words.
This matter is clear and fundamentally without concealment; true understanding does not depend on much talk.
Vast and expansive, brilliant and luminous, it is constantly manifest before one whether eyes are open or closed. The thousand hands of Great Compassion cannot cover it; it is like a lotus...
The difficulties of the womb and the prison are entangling; one is starkly naked and bare. Under the bright sun and clear sky, do not hold up a torch;
a Persian sits within a crystal jar. On the branches of the Huangbo tree hang honeyed fruits. The most wondrous among wonders, the most marvelous among marvels:
the original nature of the mind transcends the profound and subtle. At the crossroads stands the old man Liao, looking left and right as he raises his eyebrows.

A Verse on the Iron Ox Presented to the Elder Mù The iron ox is cast entirely from raw iron; its nature is uniquely distinct from that of ordinary cattle. Its nostrils are stubborn and refuse to be pierced;
its two horns point toward heaven, how towering and jagged they are! When a mosquito flies by, it finds it difficult to drop its beak; though it has ears, how could it hear?
Spring rains: pulled back, they do not yield; pushed forward, they do not advance. The young lad merely exerts his whip and cane, yet the vast fields stretch on without the plow being moved.
Looking up, the misty smoke and weeds are all the more desolate. How can we avail ourselves of this season to borrow the remaining strength?
Behold now the ripening grain, its ears arcing like rainbows.
Huanju wrote this for the Elder Jing’e Xiaohan Yin:

The three realms are towering within the illusory; the six paths are faint within the real. If one cannot yet comprehend illusion to realize non-arising, how is this different from steaming sand in hopes of making rice?
The practitioner Jing’e is truly eccentric; his ordinary wondrous functions—how could they be otherwise?
One may know this: within the horn of a snail one unfolds the world; inside the pore of a lotus fiber one hides Mount Sumeru.

A single room opens vast upon the base of a stone tower—who says that even empty space cannot contain it? The returning immortals merely boast in their own clamor, becoming attached within the gate of illusionary transformations.
Flying springs burst forth from the ravines like rolling thunder; the white moon shines upon the green lotus pedestal. All dharmas...
All is empty, the one true stillness; yet failing to glimpse the threshold of the numinous, one needlessly stirs with doubt and wonder.
Master Yuxi is styled Wenhai (Ocean of Literature); Elder Songyue composed a song for him. I have therefore followed his rhyme:
"The ocean of literature in my house is not merely vast; a single scoop can contain ten thousand deep seas. The texts of the Buddha and the classics of Lu swell its surplus."
